chunks: Do not discontinue a good tradition in which the early leaders of this community acted, by which unity was gathered, and through which the subjects prospered,
And do not innovate a tradition that harms any of those past traditions, so that the reward remains for the one who established it, and the burden of what you have discontinued falls upon you.

And increase your study sessions with the scholars, and your discussions with the wise, in stabilizing what has become sound in the affairs of your land, and in maintaining what the people had remained steadfast in before you.

key_terms.صُدُورُ الْأُمَّةِ: the early leaders/pioneers of the community

ai.seo_question: What are the key principles of governance and continuity in Imam Ali's letter to Malik al-Ashtar?
ai.summary: This passage highlights the Shia political principle of *al-Sunna al-Sahihah* (the authentic tradition), emphasizing that a ruler's legitimacy is tied to preserving the social cohesion (*al-Ulfah*) and justice established by predecessors. It introduces a nuanced accountability mechanism where the innovator bears the burden of disruption while retaining the reward for the original good practice, urging continuous scholarly consultation (*Mudarasa*) to ensure governance remains aligned with public welfare.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Do not discontinue the good lives in which the earlier people of this community had been acting, by virtue of which there was general unity and through which the subjects prospered.

Do not innovate any line of action which injures these earlier ways because (in that case) the reward for those who had established those ways will continue, but the burden for discontinuing them will be on you.

Keep on increasing your conversations with the scholars and discussions with the wise to stabilize the prosperity of the areas under you, and to continue with that in which the earlier people had remained steadfast.
